title: E.G.G.: Elemental Gimmick Gear
subtitle: A sleeper inside an ancient machine
summary: E.G.G.: Elemental Gimmick Gear is Birthday's action role-playing game, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 27 May 1999.
body: E.G.G.: Elemental Gimmick Gear is Birthday's action role-playing game, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 27 May 1999. An ancient egg-shaped machine is discovered with a sleeping man inside, beginning a mystery around the ruins of Tokion. Exploration uses hand-drawn environments seen from above, giving the landscape a detailed illustrated appearance. The machine provides the central link between that setting and the player's actions. Moving through the ruins means learning how its capabilities interact with mechanisms and obstacles left by a civilisation whose purpose has become uncertain.

Puzzles place switches, movable objects and closed passages around the route. Finding the next way forward requires inspecting their arrangement and using the machine to alter it. Racing sections change the task by rolling the protagonist into an egg-like form and sending him along rails against opponents. That movement gives the shape in the title a practical use beyond its appearance. The adventure alternates between working through a room and handling a more immediate movement challenge, keeping the equipment tied to several different kinds of progress.

Boss encounters switch from the illustrated overhead environments to three-dimensional graphics, changing the presentation when the adventure reaches a major confrontation. The discovery of the ancient machine also explains its place in the wider world: researchers studied it and produced copies for everyday use, long before the ruins became active again. That history makes the equipment both an archaeological object and something familiar to the inhabitants. The visual transition at the bosses gives those confrontations a distinct scale, while exploration returns the player to the carefully drawn spaces where the mystery began.
